stories.headline: Russia's own data show almost 500,000 deaths in Ukraine war
stories.summary: Leaked Russian figures put war deaths in Ukraine at almost 500,000, according to BBC World reporting. The data show how the full-scale invasion has changed mortality patterns inside Russia.

stories.headline: Leaked data show over 300 Russians killed supporting Mali's junta
stories.summary: A Guardian exclusive based on leaked records lists 349 Russian deaths over three years in Mali. The records also shed light on Russian military activity elsewhere in Africa.

stories.headline: Colombia's president rushes to supermarket hostage siege
stories.summary: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has arrived at an hours-long standoff in a tourist city, where gunmen are holding at least 20 people hostage inside a supermarket. He is taking control of an operation involving scores of security personnel.

stories.headline: Kilmar Ábrego García leaves US for Spain
stories.summary: The Salvadoran man, deported in March 2025 and later returned to the US after a Supreme Court ruling, has left the United States of his own volition for Spain. His lawyers confirmed the move, and the Department of Homeland Security confirmed he was travelling. His departure ends a long flashpoint in the debate over President Trump's immigration agenda.

stories.headline: China investigates Shanghai Party chief Chen Jining
stories.summary: China has launched an investigation into Chen Jining, Shanghai's Communist Party chief and a member of the elite Politburo, according to Xinhua. He is the fourth Politburo member to be investigated since 2025, and was seen as a contender for higher office.

stories.headline: Huawei convicted of trade secret theft in New York
stories.summary: A US jury found Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets and of bank fraud and money laundering conspiracy, after a months-long trial in New York. The company was acquitted of racketeering charges.

stories.headline: Israeli strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike killed Naeem Abu Nahel, Hamas's internal security chief, who had held the post for two months. He is among seven Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes on Tuesday, and a separate strike on an apartment building in Shati camp killed at least four people.

stories.headline: Asian markets fall as AI boom doubts return
stories.summary: Stocks fell sharply in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan in a tech-led sell-off. SoftBank dropped 15% as renewed concerns over the AI trade hit Asian tech names, particularly Japanese semiconductor stocks.

stories.headline: Nvidia shares fall as Huang row deepens
stories.summary: Nvidia's share price fell around 7% as lawmakers demanded answers about President Trump's role in reinstating CEO Jensen Huang. The US attorney general dodged questions on an investigation into the company. Trump said he 'convinced' the board, and reports say he made up to $15m on his Nvidia holdings.

stories.headline: Trump readies new tariffs on major trading partners
stories.summary: The US is preparing to unveil new tariffs on global trading partners, including China, the EU, Japan and South Korea. The levies would hit many of America's biggest trading partners.

stories.headline: Compass to move main listing from London to New York
stories.summary: Compass Group, the world's largest catering group, confirmed plans to move its main listing to the US, saying it had become a predominantly North American business. The move is a blow to the London Stock Exchange.

stories.headline: Energy price cap to rise in January
stories.summary: Ofgem's new energy price cap will push up domestic gas prices significantly from January. Households are bracing for higher bills, though millions are due a £100 energy payment from January.

stories.headline: Yoro red card overturned ahead of Brentford game
stories.summary: Manchester United defender Leny Yoro's red card at Anfield was overturned, so he is clear to face Brentford on Saturday. Referees' chief Howard Webb backed the original decision, while Mauricio Pochettino and United were furious over how VAR handled it.

stories.headline: England level T20 series with Australia at Carrara
stories.summary: Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt put on 150 in 10 overs, helping England chase 184 against Australia and level the T20 series. Donald's stunning onslaught was the highlight of the chase.

stories.headline: Arsenal held by Dortmund, Man City drawn with Napoli
stories.summary: Arsenal were held to a 2-2 style draw by Borussia Dortmund after leading at half-time, with Gyökeres's thunderbolt followed by Beier's equaliser. Manchester City also drew with Napoli, with Rayan Cherki's goal denying them a win in a laboured performance.

stories.headline: Ireland's Dan Sheehan banned for two games
stories.summary: Ireland's stand-in captain Dan Sheehan received a two-game ban for a croc-roll tackle against South Africa. He will miss Ireland's match against Australia on Friday night. Ireland beat back-to-back world champions South Africa in a narrow victory.

stories.headline: Ollie Robinson leaves Sussex for Nottinghamshire
stories.summary: England seamer Ollie Robinson is leaving Sussex after 11 or 12 seasons to join Nottinghamshire on a three-year deal. The move came with an undisclosed compensation package.

stories.headline: Pakistan's first astronaut launches on Chinese rocket
stories.summary: Pakistani former fighter pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali launched into space aboard China's Shenzhou-24. He is the first foreigner to join a Chinese crewed space mission.

stories.headline: Record heat-linked deaths estimated in England
stories.summary: The UK Health Security Agency estimates 5,200 heat-linked deaths in England this year, twice the previous record year. The figure is a stark measure of heat's health toll.

stories.headline: Carbon removal projects advance after COP31
stories.summary: Carbon Herald reported CO2-storing concrete deployed at the Port of Rotterdam, and a new report on the state of direct air carbon capture and storage (DACCS). A Carbon Capture Coalition package also went to the US EPA with Class VI permitting reform proposals. COP31 in Antalya ended without an agreed 'pact' on climate action.

stories.headline: Thomas Markle charged with possessing child abuse images
stories.summary: Thomas Markle, father of Meghan, has been charged in the US with possessing child sexual abuse images. The FBI arrested him on 6 November after a search of a storage unit he had allegedly rented in Los Angeles uncovered the material.

stories.headline: Nigella Lawson helps crown new Bake Off champion
stories.summary: A new Great British Bake Off winner was crowned after a high-stakes final, with Nigella Lawson describing the three finalists as sensational. Guardian coverage says viewing figures are up since her arrival as judge.

stories.headline: First Children's Booker Prize shortlist announced
stories.summary: The inaugural Children's Booker Prize shortlist has been revealed, with eight titles including works by Eoin Colfer, Shaun Tan and Liz Hyder. The award carries £50,000 and has child judges.

stories.headline: Bros announce first tour in a decade
stories.summary: Pop duo Bros will tour in 2027, with ten dates including Wembley Arena. The twins from Camberley are returning to live performance after a decade.

stories.headline: Wolbachia mosquitoes cut viral infections by 68% in Brazil
stories.summary: A large Brazilian trial that released Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes cut viral infections by 68%, with schoolchildren enjoying a lower risk of such diseases. The method uses bacteria that inhibit the insects' ability to transmit viruses.

stories.headline: Thanksgiving Heroes to serve thousands of families
stories.summary: The Thanksgiving Heroes effort, which began with an 11-year-old's promise to his mother, will feed 3,600 families in Utah alone this year. The initiative aims to bring holiday meals to those in need nationwide.

stories.headline: Micronesian school accepts coconuts for tuition
stories.summary: Faith Christian Academy in Micronesia accepts coconuts in lieu of tuition fees, easing the financial burden on families. The scheme helps every islander afford school.

stories.headline: Retired teacher's bird cafe made from old instruments
stories.summary: A retired teacher in Prince Edward Island, Canada, turns scrapped musical instruments into bird feeders at his Frets and Feathers Cafe, offering free food to birds.

stories.headline: Asteroid mission returns to assess crash damage
stories.summary: Four years after a spacecraft deliberately knocked an asteroid off course, another spacecraft has returned to study the damage. The mission is examining the asteroid's changed path.
